maml:description.maml:para: Download, validate and install the official VSO distribution.

Interactive scope and folder selection use native choices. An explicit Scope or AllUsers skips only scope selection; an interactive invocation still asks for the destination. Path alone selects CurrentUser without questions. CurrentUser uses LOCALAPPDATA; AllUsers uses ProgramFiles. GitHub release assets, archive SHA-256, extraction limits and every internal file checksum are validated before promotion. Unknown files are preserved and an existing installation requires Update or Force. Quiet never elevates. WhatIf creates no files and makes no network request.

ProcessState Unknown means visibility was insufficient; Idle only means that no attributed process was found with available evidence. Status does not check Internet updates or claim VSO finished startup. No confirmations or writes.

maml:description.maml:para: Remove owned application files while preserving Windows Recovery and unknown data.

Application and module removal are independent. Reset-VSO removes the application; Reset-VSO -Full includes additional attributable data. Uninstall-PSResource VSO removes the module, or use Uninstall-Module VSO for PowerShellGet. Neither action removes the other component. Always preview with WhatIf and PassThru. Displays exact deletion and preservation lists. Normal reset removes unchanged application files and matching registration/receipt while preserving receipted persistent data. Full also removes unchanged receipted configuration, cache, logs, temporary files and attributable transaction metadata. Protected objects include explicit ownership reasons; shared or untracked data cannot be completely cleaned. Modified and foreign files survive. Full cannot attribute VSO7 shared ProgramData or untracked runtime data to one installation, so those are preserved. RemoveBackups plus AcknowledgeBackupLoss explicitly permits deletion of owned previous application copies. Quiet/non-interactive destructive execution requires Force. Uninstalling files does not reverse any Windows tweak. The Gallery module itself remains installed.
